title: What Hidden Security Risks Threaten Your Connected Frontline?
summary: Fast-paced retail, warehouse, and transportation and logistics environments demand quick decisions. When selecting handheld mobile computers for your frontline teams, upfront price tags frequently dominate discussions.
body_markdown:
**


**Key Takeaways**


- Prioritizing initial hardware price often obscures critical vulnerabilities that inflate total cost of ownership.
- Protecting shopper information demands hardware-backed encryption and consistent OS updates.
- Mature software ecosystems deliver predictable returns while reducing burdens on IT personnel.
- Reliable global support prevents costly downtime for customer-facing teams.

## How Secure Are Your “Secure” Mobile Devices?


Bargain hardware sometimes ships with fundamental security flaws. Certain low-cost models arrive with unlocked bootloaders by default. Such configurations invite malware and allow malicious firmware execution, compromising sensitive customer profiles. Furthermore, relying on budget vendors often means accepting unpredictable patch schedules. This uncertainty forces IT teams into endless monitoring cycles, creating massive compliance headaches.


Securing enterprise networks requires robust defenses. Zebra[TC201](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/products/mobile-computers/handheld/tc2x-series.html) and[TC501](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/products/mobile-computers/handheld/tc5x-series/tc501.html) devices incorporate hardware-backed Secure Boot and Google StrongBox encryption to block unauthorized access. Our[LifeGuard™ for Android™](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/software/mobile-computer-software/lifeguard.html) software, guarantees timely OS patches.


## What Price Do Businesses Pay for Fragmented Software?


What happens after you purchase bargain hardware? A low upfront price frequently buys you a barebones consumer-grade experience lacking native deployment tools. Relying on piecemeal strategies drains productivity, as IT teams waste precious time integrating third-party staging applications just to make the units functional.


## Does Flimsy Hardware Truly Support Your Frontline?


How much value does a device offer if it fails in real-world conditions? Some manufacturers advertise impressive durability specifications that are only valid with the purchase of a separate "protective boot" or tested only in controlled room temperatures.


This approach means the device your frontline uses day-to-day may not withstand the drops, tumbles, and temperature fluctuations common in warehouses or on delivery routes. High hardware failure rates lead directly to frontline productivity loss and spike support costs.


Zebra tests products thoroughly, exceeding standard MIL-STD-810 requirements. Superior durability supports your connected frontline’s asset visibility. Food service leader[Bidfood](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/resource-library/success-stories/from-paper-to-precision-bidfoods-digital-journey-to-operational-excellence.html) experienced this firsthand, moving from paper-based systems to Zebra mobile computers to achieve new levels of operational excellence and precision in demanding environments. ****


## Can Your Support Network Prevent Costly Downtime?


When a device fails, how long must you wait for a replacement? For global businesses, operational continuity is everything. Some vendors operate fragmented regional repair centers with "return-to-base" models, where the average turnaround time stretches to seven days or more. This delay forces you to purchase and manage a bloated spare pool of up to 20% extra hardware to cover the downtime.


Zebra’s global network provides consistent, high-quality support in over 100 countries. Zebra[OneCare™](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/services/support-services/zebra-onecare-support-services.html) support offers next-business-day, "like-new" replacement devices, keeping your spare pool lean and your operations moving. Equipping operations with reliable enterprise solutions drives incredible results; for example, deploying Zebra devices enabled[DPD Austria](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/resource-library/success-stories/dpd-austria-accelerates-the-processing-of-parcels-triples-its-parcel-shop-network.html) to accelerate parcel processing and triple its parcel shop network.
